name: Lazarus Pharmaceutical Emetix-9 'Purge'
description:
The Emetix-9 is a handheld aerosol dispersal unit containing a proprietary Lazarus Pharmaceutical compound designated LP-Emetic-9, a synthetic cholinomimetic agent that binds aggressively to gastrointestinal vagal receptors and the chemoreceptor trigger zone simultaneously. Onset of violent emesis occurs within four to eight seconds of inhalation or mucosal contact, followed by sustained nausea lasting fifteen to forty minutes depending on the subject's metabolic rate and augmentation status. The compound is colorless and carries only a faint medicinal odor — subjects often have no warning before incapacitation.

Developed originally as an emergency counter-toxin delivery mechanism for Lazarus field medics, the Emetix-9 was quietly repurposed and licensed to Meridian Municipal Security for crowd dispersal after internal trials demonstrated its near-universal effectiveness across augmented and baseline human subjects alike. Unlike OC-based sprays, Emetix-9 does not rely on pain compliance — it bypasses conscious resistance entirely by triggering an involuntary physiological cascade. A subject can be enraged, armored, and pain-tolerant and still be incapacitated within seconds.

The weapon is controversial within civil liberties advocacy circles because Lazarus holds the antidote — LP-Antag-9 — under a separate licensed product, and municipal contracts have been criticized for creating dependency on Lazarus supply chains for basic crowd control operations. Street medics operating in the Shelf refer to it grimly as 'the Lazarus tax.'
legality: Licensed — municipal and licensed security use only; civilian possession requires medical dispensary license
specifications:
Active compound: LP-Emetic-9 (cholinomimetic agonist)
Delivery: pressurized aerosol cone, 1.2m spread at 2m range
Onset: 4–8 seconds post-exposure
Duration of effect: 15–40 minutes
Canister capacity: 6 bursts
Weight: 0.19 kg
Dimensions: 14cm × 4cm
Shelf life: 36 months
Antidote: LP-Antag-9 (sold separately, licensed)
Price: Φ85
tactical_use: Municipal security deploys Emetix-9 in confined crowd situations where OC spray or acoustic tools are impractical — transit hubs, elevator corridors, processing queues. A single burst into a packed crowd creates immediate secondary disruption as affected individuals involuntarily drop, collapse, or create space around themselves. Security teams are trained to deploy from upwind positions and follow immediately with physical containment while subjects are incapacitated. It is also used by licensed bounty contractors for non-damaging subject extraction — a target rendered unable to stand or resist is far easier to transport than one who has been beaten into compliance.
cultural_context: On the street, Emetix-9 is called 'Nine-Sick' or simply 'The Heave.' Shelf residents have a deep and specific hatred for it — being gassed with Purge in a protest crackdown is described as a uniquely humiliating experience, and the fact that Lazarus profits from both the weapon and its antidote is a recurring grievance in anti-corporate graffiti. Security forces using it are sometimes called 'Lazarus boys' regardless of actual employer. There is a dark irony in its medicinal origins that has not been lost on anyone.
story_hooks: A shipment of LP-Antag-9 antidote has been intercepted, and a protest is scheduled in three days — someone wants the crowd to suffer without relief

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact handheld aerosol disperser resembling a dental anesthetic injector crossed with a compact fire extinguisher. Angular, utilitarian design with a pronounced grip trigger and pressurized chamber. Clinical and pharmaceutical in appearance — designed to look medical rather than aggressive.
physical_description.dimensions: 14cm length × 4cm diameter; compact enough to fit in a jacket pocket or security belt holster
physical_description.weight_description: Lightweight and well-balanced — 0.19kg feels almost insubstantial in hand, deceptively so given its incapacitating payload. Pressurized canister has a subtle heft that belies its diminutive size.
physical_description.primary_material: Anodized aluminum pressure vessel with reinforced polymer grip housing; medical-grade stainless steel valve assembly
physical_description.finish: Matte pharmaceutical white with chrome micro-valve accents; polished steel pressure seals. Clean, sterile appearance — no weathering or battle-scars typical of this device.
physical_description.color_scheme: Clinical white primary body with metallic chrome valve housing and pressure indicator band; BrightSmile Dental Care branding in soft blue accent
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer grip with micro-texture for wet-hand security; textured to prevent fumbling under stress
distinctive_features: Pressurized micro-valve nozzle with precision cone-spread adjustment marking
Color-coded pressure indicator band (green-yellow-red) on cylinder wall
BrightSmile Dental Care logo embossed on grip — pharmaceutical branding deliberately clinical
Numbered burst counter (0-6) etched near trigger guard
Small medical cross symbol below manufacturer mark
Faint residual condensation on exterior after storage — sign of internal pressure stability
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: BrightSmile Dental Care corporate logo in soft blue on grip face; 'LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICAL LP-EMETIC-9' stamped on pressure vessel in small clinical font; holographic authenticity seal near valve; batch number and expiration date on base
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine and laboratory-clean — maintained under strict municipal/corporate protocols. Rarely field-weathered; treated as consumable medical equipment rather than personal weapon. Pressure seals kept tight; nozzle dust-capped when holstered.
